correction.title: A Synchronized Break Waits For Its Hands And Uses One Deadline

cases: Two managers persisting sequentially with two seconds of latency receive different break deadlines.
A late entrant receives a deadline two seconds beyond the existing shared deadline.
An entrant joining during the drain receives a fabricated countdown before hands finish.
An exception from a table's parked-state inspection is counted as a successful drain.
A hand reaching its boundary at 121 seconds is rejected by the 120-second grace limit.
A manager-owned synchronized break self-releases at its 420-second initial budget.

behavior: GameServer waits for all participating table boundaries until its server generation stops owning the drain.
Unknown table inspection remains unproven and cannot open the countdown.
Live and restored synchronized breaks request explicit manager release; the ordinary hand-for-hand safety timeout remains.
One absolute deadline reaches each persisted tournament countdown and the shared resume timer.
A newcomer during the drain is paused without being shown a fabricated countdown; current managers join the countdown participant set.
limits: Tests invoke actual imported runtime methods with controlled time and mocked persistence/table-boundary responses; they do not execute production settlement or payment writes.
Required CI, merged-source integration and production engine adoption remain unverified for this correction.
Complete K05 acceptance still requires integrated real-hand settlement, restart and published UI deadline evidence.

thaw_catalog_review.current_caller: The inspected GameServer uses the three-argument fn_thaw_platform overload. Presence of the newer ownership-aware overload does not prove that caller adopts its complete release contract.
thaw_catalog_review.limits: Catalog review only. No deadline row was shifted, no migration was applied and no production financial operation was invoked.

controls.requirement: Use one durable tournament clock and level definition across all tables. Restart must restore elapsed active-play time.
controls.remaining: Existing break-restart remainder behavior is verified; full durable authority and all restart/level boundaries remain.

controls.requirement: Define registration wall time separately from blind time and maintenance extensions. Test daylight saving and UTC conversion.
controls.remaining: UTC/DST cadence is already verified. Current late-registration formula and its maintenance extension contract remain unverified.

controls.requirement: Publish break cadence, duration and exceptions. Track requested, draining, on-break and resumed states explicitly.
controls.remaining: This correction distinguishes the drain from a real countdown; player-visible cadence, duration and exception publication are not fully certified.

controls.requirement: Finish active hands before a tournament break begins; release participating tables using one authoritative deadline.
controls.remaining: Integrate this correction, pass required CI, verify engine adoption and exercise the complete real-hand settlement/restart/UI boundary.

controls.requirement: Transfer all applicable deadlines across the approved maintenance freeze. No hidden time-bank, rebuy or offer expiry.
controls.remaining: Actual installed thaw behavior across all player deadlines and rolling restart callers remains unverified.

controls.requirement: Test missed scheduler ticks, engine failover and long-running hands at :53/:55/:00 without restarting active settlement.
controls.remaining: UTC missed-tick behavior and the focused 121-second drain test are covered; combined active settlement/failover scenario remains.

controls.requirement: Blind expiry, registration closure, :53 drain and :55 maintenance overlap a long hand: assigned forced bets stay fixed; each clock follows its documented policy.
controls.remaining: The combined blind/registration/drain/maintenance scenario remains; root owns the blind snapshot and pause-edge corrections.
